name: Slack

verdict.topBlocker: Unlisted apps can read message history only once a minute, so message-reading agents effectively need Marketplace approval (10+ active workspaces, then up to ~12 weeks of review).
verdict.summary: Two paths. Letting other workspaces install your app needs no Slack review: you activate public distribution and use HTTPS redirect URLs (0 days of waiting). But since 29 May 2025, unlisted commercial apps are limited to 1 request/min on conversations.history and conversations.replies, so an agent that reads messages realistically needs Marketplace approval: 10+ active workspaces first, then up to 10 business days of preliminary review and up to 10 weeks of functional review.

steps.title: Create Slack App in Development Workspace
steps.detail: Sign in to the Slack App Management console and create a new application attached to your primary development workspace.

steps.title: Configure App Manifest and Redirect URIs
steps.detail: Draft the Slack app manifest defining requested bot and user scopes, and register your server's secure HTTPS OAuth redirect URI.

steps.title: Implement OAuth Authorization Code Flow and State Validation
steps.detail: Implement the OAuth initiate endpoint with CSRF state generation and construct the authorization link pointing to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize. Create the callback handler to exchange codes via oauth.v2.access.

steps.title: Activate public distribution (no review needed)
steps.detail: Go to Settings → Manage Distribution, complete the checklist (HTTPS redirect, interactivity and event URLs; no hard-coded tokens) and click 'Activate Public Distribution'. Any workspace can now install the app through OAuth — no Slack approval. Each customer's workspace admin may still need to approve the install.

steps.title: Run Automated OAuth Flow and Token Refresh Verification
steps.detail: Run test authorization flows to confirm state verification, access token exchange, and refresh token rotation logic.

steps.title: (Marketplace path) Reach 10+ active workspaces
steps.detail: Marketplace submission requires the app to be installed and active on at least 10 workspaces within the last 28 days. Slack doesn't say whether your own test workspaces count; real customer installs are the safe assumption.

steps.title: (Marketplace path) Draft Listing Information and Record Demo Video
steps.detail: Draft short/long app descriptions, collect support contact links, and record a walkthrough video showing installation, scope prompts, feature usage, and uninstallation.

steps.title: (Marketplace path) Submit App to Slack Marketplace with Test Credentials
steps.detail: Open 'Submit to the Slack Marketplace' in app settings, enter app details, provide test account logins for testing, and submit for review.

steps.title: (Marketplace path) Wait for Slack Preliminary Review
steps.detail: Slack Marketplace reviewers conduct a preliminary check on listing completeness, links, and scope justifications. Resubmissions during this phase reset queue placement.

steps.title: (Marketplace path) Wait for Slack Functional Review
steps.detail: An assigned reviewer performs end-to-end testing of app features, OAuth flows, and restricted scope compliance. New submissions take up to 10 weeks.

steps.title: (Marketplace path) Publish App on Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Once approved, publish the app live on the Slack Marketplace for public customer discovery and installation.

requirements.note: A Slack account and development workspace are required to create and test Slack applications.
A valid Privacy Policy URL must be provided for Marketplace listing review.
Terms of Service compliance and documentation are required during Marketplace submission.
A short video showcasing installation, OAuth consent, features, and uninstallation is strongly recommended to assist functional review.
The app must be installed on at least 10 active workspaces used within the last 28 days before submission is unblocked.

scopes.note: Standard bot scope for sending channel messages.
Accessing message history in public channels triggers enhanced review.
Admin scopes trigger enhanced review and are generally unsuitable without clear justification.
Broad search access triggers enhanced review and requires explicit justification.

blockers.symptom: Your agent's message reads are throttled to 1 request per minute, 15 messages per call, in customer workspaces.
blockers.cause: Since 29 May 2025, commercially distributed apps not approved for the Slack Marketplace get Tier 1 limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies (internal apps are exempt).
blockers.unblock: Plan for Marketplace approval early (it needs 10 active workspaces plus up to ~12 weeks of review), or design the agent around events and posting rather than reading history.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission blocked in developer dashboard.
blockers.cause: The app has fewer than 10 active workspace installations active within the past 28 days.
blockers.unblock: Distribute your app install link directly to at least 10 active workspaces and gather active user usage before submitting.

blockers.symptom: OAuth flow fails returning bad_redirect_uri error during installation.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri passed in authorization or token exchange does not match the URI registered under OAuth & Permissions.
blockers.unblock: Ensure the exact HTTPS redirect URI is listed under Redirect URLs in Slack app settings.

blockers.symptom: Preliminary review timeline repeatedly resets, delaying app launch.
blockers.cause: Making edits or resubmitting information during the preliminary review phase resets your queue position back to the start.
blockers.unblock: Ensure all listing copy, URLs, and documentation are completely finalized before submitting to avoid mid-review edits.

blockers.symptom: App submission rejected due to scope permissions.
blockers.cause: Requesting broad or restricted scopes (such as admin.* or search:read) without clear documented use cases.
blockers.unblock: Remove unnecessary sensitive scopes or provide detailed written and video documentation justifying their necessity.

gaps: Specific financial costs or fees for Slack Marketplace developer accounts are not detailed in the sources.
reviewNote: Review corrected the agent's verdict, which treated the Marketplace as mandatory (difficulty 4, wait 14–84 days). Public distribution needs no review. We kept difficulty 4 with a 0–84 day range because the 2025 rate limits make Marketplace approval effectively required for message-reading AI agents; apps that only post messages can stop at public distribution (difficulty 2, no wait).
